- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.2), model underreacts to mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast mean for next 5–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) true values; apply 1.5–3% upward adjustment to final 5–7 forecast points if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transitions using 3-day weighted average of sentiment.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model overestimates recovery; reduce forecast mean by 1–3% for next 5 days, especially if price is above 85% of 30-day high.
